value.first: Nights 1-3: set up her room first so it feels like hers before she has to sleep in it. Let her help pick where the bed goes, do the whole bedtime routine there, and stay the first few nights, sitting beside her bed until she is asleep. At 2 the goal is just teaching her the new room is safe, not distance yet. Expect protest and some tears the first night or two. That is normal and not a sign it is failing.
value.second: Nights 4-7: keep the routine identical but move your chair a little toward the door each night, maybe a foot or two, and drop from talking to just a quiet hand on her back. When she wakes and comes to you, walk her straight back with as little chat as possible, every time. Toddlers test hardest around night 3 or 4 once they realize the setup changed, so a rough middle stretch usually means it is working, not backfiring.
value.third: After that: you are near the door or just outside, still returning her calmly each time she gets up. Most families see the new room settle in a week or two of staying consistent. Signs it is working: fewer wakings, quicker resettling, less protest at the routine. If she is still waking multiple times a night with real distress after about two weeks of a steady routine, that is worth raising with your doctor.
